title: Air India Says US Flights Ran On Schedule Despite Ground Stop
excerpt: In a Saturday-evening update reversing its earlier delay warning, Air India said its New York, Newark and San Francisco flights landed and departed on time — with one documented exception, a San Francisco departure more than three hours late.
body:
• Air India said on Saturday, November 14, 2026, that all its flights to and from the United States operated as per schedule without any significant delay, despite the FAA's nationwide ground stop.
  • The airline said its flights en route to New York, Newark and San Francisco landed on time early on Saturday, and departures from those three airports were also on time.
  • One exception is documented: Air India's San Francisco flight AI184, scheduled to depart at 6:35 p.m. on Friday, took off more than three hours late at 10 p.m., according to flight-tracking data reported by The Hindu BusinessLine.
  • For travellers: the wider U.S. system is still disrupted, with more than 2,500 flights cancelled on Saturday, so check your specific flight status before leaving for the airport even if your Air India long-haul leg is on time.
Operating, with one documented delay: Air India's long-haul U.S. services ran on schedule on Saturday, November 14, 2026, according to the airline. One U.S. departure, AI184 from San Francisco on Friday evening, left more than three hours late. U.S. domestic connections remain heavily disrupted.

Air India has updated its position on the FAA ground stop. In a statement reported on Saturday evening, the airline said all its flights to and from the United States have been operating as per schedule without any significant delay, even as air traffic across the U.S. was severely affected by the nationwide ground stop imposed on Friday afternoon because of communications problems at regional air traffic control centres, according to the syndicated Business Standard report.

"All our flights to and from the US have been operating as per schedule without any significant delay in spite of air traffic getting severely impacted due to the nationwide ground stop in the USA since last night."

— Air India

The statement is a material change from the airline's earlier position on Saturday, when it warned passengers of possible consequential disruptions to its U.S. flights and advised them to check their flight status. The airline now says its flights en route to New York, Newark and San Francisco landed on time early on Saturday morning, and that departures from those three airports were also on time without any significant delay. Air India is the only Indian carrier operating services to and from the United States.

The One Documented Exception

The on-schedule picture is not complete. The Hindu BusinessLine, citing Flightradar24 data, reported that Air India's San Francisco–Kolkata–Delhi flight AI184, scheduled to depart at 6:35 p.m. on Friday, took off more than three hours late at 10 p.m. An Air India official told the paper there was no significant impact on its U.S. operations, with only one flight leaving late, and that outbound flights from Mumbai and Delhi to the U.S. left in the early hours of Saturday.

https://www.instagram.com/reel/Dfhi15iB_IP/

Other India-bound services were hit harder. American Airlines' New York–Delhi flight AA292 on Friday night was cancelled, and United's Newark–Delhi flight UA82 departed about an hour behind schedule, according to the same report.

The Wider U.S. Disruption

Air India's long-haul operations held up against a severe national backdrop. More than 2,500 flights were cancelled in the United States on Saturday and hundreds more were delayed, according to FlightAware figures cited in the Business Standard report, while The Hindu BusinessLine put the total at nearly 10,000 flights delayed or cancelled through Saturday. The FAA lifted the ground stop after testing its systems, and U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the outages were caused by an overload of an old analog system, with no evidence of a cyberattack.

Before you travel

  • Check your specific flight status before leaving for the airport: Air India's on-schedule statement covers its long-haul services, and U.S. domestic connections are still facing cancellations.
  • Allow extra time if you are connecting through a U.S. hub, where residual delays from Friday's ground stop continue through Saturday.
  • If you are booked on AI184 or another Friday-evening U.S. departure, confirm the revised timing with the airline rather than relying on the original schedule.

What to Watch

The remaining question is connections, not the long-haul legs themselves. If U.S. cancellations stay elevated into Sunday, India-bound passengers connecting from domestic U.S. flights remain the group most exposed, even with Air India's transatlantic and transpacific services departing on time.
